key_insight: Nirsevimab was associated with 78.1% effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalization in eligible high-risk children aged 8–23 months entering their second RSV season.
clinical_relevance: The findings support protection against severe RSV in this eligible population; the study concerns RSV prevention, not AI or cancer drug discovery.
method: Retrospective test-negative case-control study across 26 hospitals in 24 U.S. states during the 2024–2025 and 2025–2026 RSV seasons.
Compared prior nirsevimab receipt in RSV-positive and RSV-negative children hospitalized with respiratory symptoms.
Adjusted logistic regression for age, hospitalization month and year, census region, and sex.
evidence_signal: Among 106 RSV-positive cases and 125 RSV-negative controls, nirsevimab receipt was 19.8% versus 42.4%; adjusted effectiveness was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%–89.3%).
watch_item: The small observational sample, dominated by children with chronic lung disease of prematurity, limits generalizability and may retain residual confounding.
paper_title: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV hospitalizations in children 8-23 months at risk of severe RSV
